1. tools/check_labels_v2.py (the format checker, the same file for both teams). sha256 a3a3d6654cdfacd99c4b8066924aaa77f0897caeadd9f561ae03bb57b7fa07e1, 64,846 bytes, 1,162 lines.
- It checks ONE team's record for ONE passage. It reads form only. It never says a role is right or wrong.
- Checks: R0 (the record as a whole: one JSON object, the right passage_id, "entries" is a list of objects, none_of_these true means no entries) and C1 to C9 exactly as the spec's section THE CHECKER lists them. C1 allowed values and combinations. C2 support is an exact copy, is widened to whole sentences, at most 4. C3 label is an exact copy, 1 to 12 words, inside the support; a ^1 label is located at the first place the name occurs in the passage. C4 measure only for ^4 and ^7, inside the support. C5 mind equals the label of this record's own ^1 entry. C6 relative_to per Noetic (a pair must point at each other with the same mind, certainty and hold code; a ^6 whole is an exact copy of 1 to 12 words, or empty with clue true). C7 the pointer check with the spec's closed lists, skipped with no_fuller_name true. C8 no duplicate by the scorer's own same-reading test; the later entry fails. C9 the feeling-word question for ^2 and ^3: asked once per label, never a rejection, the same label sent again is accepted.
- Every message names the entry, the check and what to do. Example: "entry 5 (^4, label 'the rattle of the tram outside'): C3. label is not an exact, unbroken copy of passage text. ... Only the capital letters differ. The passage has: 'The rattle of the tram outside'."
- The three tries are one function, take_try. Team B's tool calls it. Team A reaches it through the command line. Accepted on a try: final. After the third try the third record is final; each entry that still fails C1 to C8 is DROPPED and stays in the record with marks. If the third try gives no readable record the passage is NOT LABELED.
- Command line. Plain check (nothing counted): check_labels_v2.py PASSAGES LABELS. Counted try: check_labels_v2.py PASSAGES RECORD --tries LOG [--id ID]. Final labels file: check_labels_v2.py PASSAGES --export OUT --tries LOG [LOG ...] [--close-unfinished]. Exit codes: 0 pass or accepted; 1 a check failed, try again; 3 final with dropped entries or not labeled; 2 the command was wrong (never a try).
- Importable: check_record(passage_text, record, passage_id, c9_asked), take_try, new_state, describe, final_row, export_rows, summarize, count_tries, and the text rules (clean, split_sentences, Passage, entry_class).
- The team A recipe is the first thing in the module docstring (8 numbered steps: one passage per file, run with --tries, read the exit code, three tries, C9 is a question, never run it without --tries, hand back the try log).
- The final labels file carries the marks tools/verdict_v2.py reads: on a dropped entry "dropped": true and "failed_checks"; on the row "labeler_failed": true (only when not labeled), "reasks" (one item per failed check per try sent back), and a "checker" block (tries, final status, dropped list).

2. tools/label_outside_v2.py (team B through an outside service). sha256 5ff159a10b42ed0eca683b47fc8024cb9546a4ecf83bc3bb8c22d34010320970, 22,092 bytes, 395 lines.
- Usage: label_outside_v2.py <provider> <model> <guide.md> <instructions.txt> <passages.json> <output.json> [seconds_between_calls] [workers] [--token-cap N] [--dry-run] [--expect-checker-sha256 HEX].
- One passage per call, temperature 0, threads, checkpoint, resume. It sends one fixed line, the guide, the labeler instructions and one passage. On another try it sends the model's own earlier reply and the checker's lines (the same lines team A reads).
- The key comes from the environment variable DEEPSEEK_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY at run time. The tool opens no key file. Error texts are scrubbed. Only the variable NAME goes into the receipt.
- It takes only id and text from the passage file and refuses a passage file with any other field (kind, setting) or with HIDDEN, KIND or BRIEF in its name. It has no input for the other team's labels or for the brief.
- A network error is not a try. Every try is written to a journal line at once, so a killed run cannot give a passage a fourth try. A finished passage is never asked again on resume.
- It writes <output>, <output>.tries.json (every try: raw reply, checker messages, what was sent back, token counts) and <output>.receipt.json (hashes of guide, instructions, passages, checker, tool; counts; tokens).

Support. The task line says 'support is whole sentences'. Spec check C2 says: exact copy, then the program widens it to whole sentences, at most 4. I followed C2. Half a sentence is widened, not refused. Each entry reports support_widened.

Entries that lean on each other. When a ^1 entry fails a check, every entry that names that Mind fails C5. When one member of a pair fails, the other fails C6. The spec's C5 and C6 do not spell this out. The scorer tools/verdict_v2.py (another builder's file) drops such entries when it locates them. I mirrored it, so the labeler is told during its tries and nothing is dropped silently. Checked on 4,000 damaged records: 0 differences.
